title: President Trump Makes an Announcement, Oct. 7, 2026
summary: White House Trump Accounts event: Bessent blames high headline inflation on the energy shock with core near target, Trump predicts oil will crash when the Iran war ends and credits tariffs for a factory boom.

assertions.quote: headline inflation is high because of the energy shock
The core inflation actually dropped last month and is approaching the Fed's target.

verdicts.note: Core CPI was 2.4% in August and 2.6% in September 2026, not far from 2%, but core PCE, the Fed's preferred gauge, ran about 3.2%.

Core CPI rose 2.6% in the 12 months to September 2026, up from 2.4% in August and 0.6 point above the 2% target (which is set on PCE inflation, usually a few tenths below CPI); the FOMC on September 16 still described inflation as elevated and raised rates.

assertions.quote: once we get on the other side of this Iran conflict, energy markets are going to be well supplied
oil will come down to levels that were, I think, maybe even lower than they were before the war started
it's a real rate issue. So it's because of growth. Growth here is strong.

verdicts.note: Growth is one driver, but the Fed chair also cites competition for capital and geopolitical commodity risk, and inflation above target lifts nominal yields too.

assertions.quote: these companies are building massive plants, all because of tariffs

verdicts.note: Some announced reshoring is real, but manufacturing employment fell in 2025 and tariff-exposed industries grew more slowly than lightly tariffed ones.

assertions.quote: We have the greatest growth of any country, maybe ever in history

verdicts.note: US real GDP growth of roughly 2-4% is far below historical episodes such as China's decade of 10% growth.
Real GDP grew at annual rates of 2.5% in Q1 and 2.2% in Q2 2026, ordinary trend-like growth, nowhere near a historical record.

assertions.quote: we've been losing, on average, $80 billion to $90 billion a year with Canada

verdicts.note: A trade deficit is goods received in exchange for payment, not a loss; economists do not treat bilateral deficits as transfers.

assertions.quote: Since the election, US stock markets have set all-time records

verdicts.note: Several autumn 2026 sources describe equities at or near record levels.
